summary: U.S. markets tumbled Tuesday after October CPI data came in hotter than expected, reigniting fears of another Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Headline inflation rose 0.4% month-over-month versus the 0.3% consensus, while core CPI climbed 0.3% against expectations for 0.2%. Fed Governor Christopher Waller signaled openness to a quarter-point December hike and floated the possibility of a half-point move if inflation remains elevated. The S&P 500 fell roughly 1% intraday, short-dated Treasury yields jumped 20 basis points to 4.76%, and money markets now price in 28 basis points of tightening for the December FOMC meeting. Bitcoin ETFs extended their bleed, losing $201 million Monday as BlackRock's IBIT marked its seventh straight day of outflows, totaling $1.66 billion over the streak. Nvidia shares dropped more than 3% and weighed heavily on tech, while Microsoft slid after Anthropic unveiled workplace tools that compete directly with Office. Earnings season is winding down, with CoreWeave and Applied Materials reporting this week amid a sharp post-earnings rotation out of AI plays.

signals.title: October CPI exceeds estimates, pressuring stocks and bonds
signals.desc: Headline CPI rose 0.4% vs 0.3% expected and core up 0.3% vs 0.2%, pushing two-year yields up 20 bps and lifting December Fed hike odds to 28 bps.

signals.title: Fed's Waller backs December quarter-point hike, floats half-point option
signals.desc: Waller said he would support at least a 25-bp hike in December and suggested a 50-bp move if inflation data does not improve, rattling risk assets.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs post seventh straight day of outflows totaling $1.66B
signals.desc: BlackRock's IBIT lost $213M Monday, extending cumulative withdrawals to $1.66B since Oct. 30 as rising rate expectations weigh on crypto demand.

signals.title: Microsoft shares drop after Anthropic unveils Office-competing tools
signals.desc: Anthropic announced Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data products that rival Microsoft Office, pressuring MSFT shares midday amid its IPO filing.

signals.title: Nvidia slides 3% as tech rotation accelerates post-CPI
signals.desc: NVDA fell despite Monday's 4% Nasdaq rally, acting as the heaviest S&P 500 drag as investors rotate out of high-multiple AI plays into defensives.

verdict: Hot CPI and hawkish Fed rhetoric have markets bracing for tighter policy into year-end, with risk assets under pressure and defensive rotation gaining momentum.
